requirement: Count words across many documents in parallel Celery tasks and merge the partial counts in a chord callback into a ranked top list.
skeleton: A count_words task, a merge_counts callback that sums and ranks, and word_report building a chord with the callback signature bound to top.
caption: A Celery map-reduce word count using celery Celery and chord, re and collections Counter, with an eager in-memory app. count_words is a task that counts lower-cased words in one document; merge_counts is the chord callback that sums every header result and returns the top words as [word, count] pairs, ties broken alphabetically. word_report raises ValueError for an empty document list or a top below 1 and returns chord(header, merge_counts.s(top=top)). The fixture asserts the merged ranking across documents, the top limit, alphabetical tie breaking, case folding and the ValueError cases.

plan.intent: Map-reduce word counts with a chord
constraints: Every header result is summed, not just the last one
Ties in count are ordered alphabetically
An empty document list raises ValueError

rationale.teaches: Build a header of task signatures, pass the list of results to a callback signature with partial kwargs, and reduce with Counter.update.
rationale.why: A callback that overwrites instead of accumulating, or ranks without a tie breaker, gives results that depend on task order.

ops.docstring: Fan word counting out over Celery tasks and merge them in a chord callback.

candidates.why_wrong: Each document's counts replace the running total instead of adding.
Tied words keep insertion order instead of alphabetical order.
One extra word beyond the requested top is returned.
Upper-case words are dropped because text is not lower-cased.
An empty document list builds an empty chord instead of raising ValueError.
